The terrestrial vertebrates of Greenland include the [Greenland dog](/wiki/Greenland_dog "Greenland dog"), which was introduced by the [Inuit](/wiki/Inuit "Inuit"), as well as [European](/wiki/Ethnic_groups_in_Europe "Ethnic groups in Europe")-introduced species such as [Greenlandic sheep](/wiki/Greenlandic_sheep "Greenlandic sheep"), goats, cattle, [reindeer](/wiki/Reindeer "Reindeer"), horse, chicken and [sheepdog](/wiki/Sheepdog "Sheepdog"), all descendants of animals imported by Europeans. [Marine mammals](/wiki/Marine_mammals "Marine mammals") include the [hooded seal](/wiki/Hooded_seal "Hooded seal") (*Cystophora cristata*) as well as the [grey seal](/wiki/Grey_seal "Grey seal") (*Halichoerus grypus*).[[149]](#cite_note-brit1911-156) Whales frequently pass very close to Greenland's shores in the late summer and early autumn. Whale species include the [beluga whale](/wiki/Beluga_whale "Beluga whale"), [blue whale](/wiki/Blue_whale "Blue whale"), [Greenland whale](/wiki/Bowhead_whale "Bowhead whale"), [fin whale](/wiki/Fin_whale "Fin whale"), [humpback whale](/wiki/Humpback_whale "Humpback whale"), [minke whale](/wiki/Minke_whale "Minke whale"), [narwhal](/wiki/Narwhal "Narwhal"), [pilot whale](/wiki/Pilot_whale "Pilot whale"), [sperm whale](/wiki/Sperm_whale "Sperm whale").[[150]](#cite_note-guide-157)

As of 2009, 269 species of fish from over 80 different families are known from the waters surrounding Greenland. Ron is introduced in the first novel in the series, *[Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone](/wiki/Harry_Potter_and_the_Philosopher%27s_Stone "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone")* (1997). He and his family encounter [Harry Potter](/wiki/Harry_Potter_(character) "Harry Potter (character)") at [King's Cross](/wiki/London_King%27s_Cross_railway_station "London King's Cross railway station") station and help him find the [Hogwarts Express](/wiki/Hogwarts_Express "Hogwarts Express"). Once aboard the train, Ron and Harry meet [Hermione Granger](/wiki/Hermione_Granger "Hermione Granger"), whom they initially dislike. At [Hogwarts](/wiki/Hogwarts "Hogwarts"), all three students are assigned to [Gryffindor](/wiki/Gryffindor "Gryffindor") House. After Ron and Harry save Hermione from a [troll](/wiki/Troll "Troll"), they develop a friendship with her.[[4]](#cite_note-5) When the trio seeks the [Philosopher's Stone](/wiki/Magical_objects_in_Harry_Potter#Philosopher's_stone "Magical objects in Harry Potter"), Ron uses his skill at [Wizard's Chess](/wiki/Magical_objects_in_Harry_Potter#Wizard's_Chess "Magical objects in Harry Potter") to allow Harry and Hermione to proceed safely through a dangerous, life-sized chess game.[[5]](#cite_note-6) At the last dinner of the school year, the Hogwarts headmaster [Albus Dumbledore](/wiki/Albus_Dumbledore "Albus Dumbledore") rewards Ron's chess skill by giving him fifty House points, which helps Gryffindor win the House Cup.[[6]](#cite_note-7)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Italia_1494-it.svg/250px-Italia_1494-it.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Italia_1494-it.svg)

Monaco (as part of the Republic of Genoa) in 1494

In 1419, the Grimaldi family purchased Monaco from the Crown of Aragon and became the official and undisputed rulers of "the Rock of Monaco". In 1612, [Honoré II](/wiki/Honor%C3%A9_II "Honoré II") began to style himself "Prince" of Monaco.[[32]](#cite_note-35) In the 1630s, he sought French protection against the Spanish forces and, in 1642, was received at the court of [Louis XIII](/wiki/Louis_XIII "Louis XIII") as a "duc et pair étranger".[[33]](#cite_note-monacoangebote.de-36)

The princes of Monaco became vassals of the French kings while at the same time remaining sovereign princes. Though successive princes and their families spent most of their lives in [Paris](/wiki/Paris "Paris"), and intermarried with French and Italian nobilities, the House of Grimaldi is of Genoese origin. The principality continued its existence as a protectorate of France until the [French Revolution](/wiki/French_Revolution "French Revolution").[[34]](#cite_note-37)

Vaduz, Liechtenstein

With a population of 41,232 as of 2023,[[5]](#cite_note-auto-5) Liechtenstein is [Europe's fourth-smallest country](/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_population "List of European countries by population") after [Vatican City](/wiki/Vatican_City "Vatican City"), [San Marino](/wiki/San_Marino "San Marino") and [Monaco](/wiki/Monaco "Monaco"). Its population is primarily [Alemannic](/wiki/Alemannic_German "Alemannic German")-speaking, although one third is foreign-born, primarily German speakers from [Germany](/wiki/Germany "Germany"), [Austria](/wiki/Austria "Austria"), and [Switzerland](/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland"), along with other Swiss, Italians, and [Turks](/wiki/Turkish_people "Turkish people"). Foreign-born people make up two-thirds of the country's workforce.[[119]](#cite_note-119)

Liechtensteiners have an average life expectancy at birth of 82.0 years, subdividing as male: 79.8 years, female: 84.8 years (2018 est.). The infant mortality rate is 4.2 per 1,000 live births, according to 2018 estimates.

Great Wall of China :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
The **Great Wall of China** ([traditional Chinese](/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): 萬里長城; [simplified Chinese](/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): 万里长城; [pinyin](/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): *Wànlǐ Chángchéng*, literally "ten thousand [*li*](/wiki/Li_(unit) "Li (unit)") long wall") is a series of [fortifications](/wiki/Fortifications "Fortifications") in China. They were built across the historical northern borders of [ancient Chinese states](/wiki/Ancient_Chinese_states "Ancient Chinese states") and [Imperial China](/wiki/Imperial_China "Imperial China") as protection against [various nomadic groups](/wiki/Eurasian_nomads "Eurasian nomads") from the [Eurasian Steppe](/wiki/Eurasian_Steppe "Eurasian Steppe"). The first walls date to the 7th century BC; these were joined together in the [Qin dynasty](/wiki/Qin_dynasty "Qin dynasty").[[4]](#cite_note-nyt-4)[[5]](#cite_note-Brit-5) Successive dynasties expanded the wall system; the best-known sections were built by the [Ming dynasty](/wiki/Ming_dynasty "Ming dynasty") (1368–1644).

To aid in defense, the Great Wall utilized [watchtowers](/wiki/Watchtower "Watchtower"), troop barracks, garrison stations, signaling capabilities through the means of smoke or fire, and its status as a transportation corridor. Other purposes of the Great Wall have included [border controls](/wiki/Border_control "Border control") (allowing control of immigration and emigration, and the imposition of duties on goods transported along the [Silk Road](/wiki/Silk_Road "Silk Road")), and the regulation of trade.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

The collective fortifications constituting the Great Wall stretch from [Liaodong](/wiki/Liaodong_Peninsula "Liaodong Peninsula") in the east to [Lop Lake](/wiki/Lop_Nur "Lop Nur") in the west, and from the present-day [Sino-Russian border](/wiki/China%E2%80%93Russia_border "China–Russia border") in the north

In December 2004, Drew signed a five-year, $55 million contract with the [Los Angeles Dodgers](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers"),[[12]](#cite_note-12) which included an escape clause after the second year. Roughly halfway through the 2005 season, Drew's season was again cut short after being hit on the wrist by a pitch from [Arizona Diamondbacks](/wiki/Arizona_Diamondbacks "Arizona Diamondbacks")' pitcher [Brad Halsey](/wiki/Brad_Halsey "Brad Halsey").

On September 18, 2006, Drew was part of only the (then) fourth-ever set of back-to-back-to-back-to-back home runs with fellow Dodgers [Jeff Kent](/wiki/Jeff_Kent "Jeff Kent"), [Russell Martin](/wiki/Russell_Martin_(baseball) "Russell Martin (baseball)"), and [Marlon Anderson](/wiki/Marlon_Anderson "Marlon Anderson").[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In 2006, Drew exercised his contract opt-out clause, forgoing $33 million over the next three years to become a [free agent](/wiki/Free_agent "Free agent"). Dodgers general manager [Ned Colletti](/wiki/Ned_Colletti "Ned Colletti") said in a teleconference that he was "surprised how it came down. Everything we had heard, everything that had been written led us to believe the player loved being here."[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) This was especially a surprise because a few days before, Drew had told an *[LA Times](/wiki/LA_Times "LA Times")* columnist on how happy he was in LA and that he was looking forward to the upcoming 2007 season. Drew had a very good season, batting .284 with 20 home runs and 100 RBI.

The [Cold War](/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") fueled a closely followed development of launch systems by the two states, resulting in the so-called [Space Race](/wiki/Space_Race "Space Race") and its later phase the Moon Race, accelerating efforts and interest in [exploration of the Moon](/wiki/Exploration_of_the_Moon "Exploration of the Moon").

Clearly visible is [Mare Moscoviense](/wiki/Mare_Moscoviense "Mare Moscoviense") (top right) and a mare triplet of [Mare Crisium](/wiki/Mare_Crisium "Mare Crisium"), [Mare Marginis](/wiki/Mare_Marginis "Mare Marginis") and [Mare Smythii](/wiki/Mare_Smythii "Mare Smythii") (left center).

After the first spaceflight of [Sputnik 1](/wiki/Sputnik_1 "Sputnik 1") in 1957 during [International Geophysical Year](/wiki/International_Geophysical_Year "International Geophysical Year") the spacecraft of the Soviet Union's [*Luna* program](/wiki/Luna_programme "Luna programme") were the first to accomplish a number of goals. fanoutqa_039725.x:
Charles E. Leiserson :: Work career :: Cilk programming language :: chunk_0002
He developed the [Cilk](/wiki/Cilk "Cilk") language for multithreaded programming, which uses a provably good [work-stealing](/wiki/Work-stealing "Work-stealing") algorithm for scheduling. His bio lists two internationally recognized chess playing programs based on Cilk, the StarSocrates and the Cilkchess.[[4]](#cite_note-bio-4)

:   See [Cilk](/wiki/Cilk "Cilk") for details on the programming language

Following this, he was founder and chief technology officer of the Cilk Arts, Inc. startup, developing Cilk-based technology for [multicore computing](/wiki/Multi-core_(computing) "Multi-core (computing)") applications. The company was acquired by [Intel](/wiki/Intel "Intel") in 2009, upon which Leiserson initiated the open source OpenCilk movement.[[4]](#cite_note-bio-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

Leiserson received multiple research awards in 2013 and 2014 for the Cilk work (see below).

He was formerly director of research and director of system architecture for [Akamai Technologies](/wiki/Akamai_Technologies "Akamai Technologies") in [Boston](/wiki/Boston "Boston"), a company that developed [content distribution networks](/wiki/Content_distribution_network "Content distribution network") in the late 1990s. The company grew out of the research made at M.I.T., and where his Ph.D. student Robert Blumofe was Executive Vice President.[[6]](#cite_note-kenkennedy-6)

Leiserson coauthored the standard algorithms textbook *[Introduction to Algorithms](/wiki/Introduction_to_Algorithms "Introduction to Algorithms")* together with [Thomas H. Cormen](/wiki/Thomas_H._Cormen "Thomas H. Cormen"), [Ronald L. Rivest](/wiki/Ronald_L._Rivest "Ronald L. Rivest"), and [Clifford Stein](/wiki/Clifford_Stein "Clifford Stein"). fanoutqa_012845.t: Robert Burns Woodward :: Research and career :: Death :: chunk_0007
fanoutqa_012845.x:
Robert Burns Woodward :: Research and career :: Death :: chunk_0007
Woodward died in [Cambridge, Massachusetts](/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts"), from a [heart attack](/wiki/Myocardial_infarction "Myocardial infarction") in his sleep.[[3]](#cite_note-:1-3)[[1]](#cite_note-formemrs-1) At the time, he was working on the synthesis of an [antibiotic](/wiki/Antibiotic "Antibiotic"), [erythromycin](/wiki/Erythromycin "Erythromycin"). A student of his said about him:[[3]](#cite_note-:1-3)

:   *I owe a lot to R. B. Woodward. He showed me that one could attack difficult problems without a clear idea of their outcome, but with confidence that intelligence and effort would solve them. He showed me the beauty of modern organic chemistry, and the relevance to the field of detailed careful reasoning. He showed me that one does not need to specialize. Woodward made great contributions to the strategy of synthesis, to the deduction of difficult structures, to the invention of new chemistry, and to theoretical aspects as well. He taught his students by example the satisfaction that comes from total immersion in our science. I treasure the memory of my association with this remarkable chemist.*
